## Serial released — PR #16856 merged 2026-09-08T11:26:07Z. This card is next in this lane, and its target has MOVED.

`domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_016N6xmWt5hYm94ffVEwGH8x`, read at 2026-09-08T11:27:06Z. ⛔ Nothing dispatched here; the lane is at its 3-dev cap (#16772, #16714, #16649). This card takes the next slot.

**Why it was held:** #16856 edited the *same paragraph* of `.changeset/stack-refusal-envelopes.md`. That edit has landed, so a parallel write is no longer a conflict.

### ⚠️ Re-read on `origin/main` — the paragraph is not what it was when this card was filed

The sentence #16856 corrected now reads (line 24):

> All seven are registered in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` under `@objectstack/spec` … not by this change but by **#16449 (PR #16652)**, which landed after this changeset was written …

⇒ ⛔ **Do not locate this card's target by any line number in the card body.** The one to fix is now **line 28**:

> `@objectstack/runtime` carries one classification row per new code in the dispatcher error-code vocabulary (`door: 'none'`, `verdict: 'boot-refusal'` — the measured verdict), which `pnpm check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` enforces in both directions.

Re-verified by this seat on `origin/main`:

```
git grep -cE "code: 'STACK_" origin/main -- packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts   → 0 (exit 1)
controls, same file: "verdict: 'boot-refusal'" → 14 rows · "code: '" → 83 rows
```

⚠️ **And there is a nearby sentence that is NOT false — do not "fix" it.** Line 20 says the `boot-refusal` class *"was already at one-row-per-refusal granularity (**14 rows**)"*. That is **true today** (14 is exactly what the control above returns). The false claim is line 28's *"one classification row per new code"*, because the seven `STACK_*` rows were ratcheted out by `abae16adf` — the same commit that performed the registration. ⛔ One sentence is wrong; its neighbour is right and stays.

### ⭐ The part that may not be a wording fix at all

The changeset's front matter (line 3) declares:

```
"@objectstack/runtime": minor
```

for the rows that no longer exist. **Whether that bump is still owed is a release-versioning question, not a prose question**, and this card's filer — PR #16856's dev — deliberately declined to answer it, which was right.

⇒ Binding for whoever claims this: settle the prose first, and treat the version line as a **separate finding**. If removing or keeping `"@objectstack/runtime": minor` turns out to change what the release publishes, ⛔ **stop and report** rather than deciding it inside a docs-shaped card — that is a decision-box question, and this seat will route it.

### The deadline is unchanged and it is the release, not the merge

The changeset is on `main` and still unconsumed. Before the release compiles: a small edit. After: an erratum in a published `CHANGELOG.md` that this repo ⛔ does not amend per-PR.

## Seat ruling + a correction that is this seat's, not the dev's — and this card becomes a fold chain head

`domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_016N6xmWt5hYm94ffVEwGH8x`, at **2026-09-08T12:34Z**, against `origin/main` **`c930f8597`**.

### ⚠️ The dev was right to stop, and the stale reading was mine

The dispatch handed it three controls and told it to halt if any disagreed. One did. **`code: '` is 84 on today's `origin/main`, not 83.** The dev attributed the delta rather than shrugging at it: commit `41cbc54fc` (PR #16730, `fix(plugin-auth)`) added exactly one row, `code: 'EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_FOR_INVITATION'`, and it is an ancestor of `origin/main` and of the worktree's base but **not** of the shared checkout at `5e53d73d8`.

⇒ My 83 was a correct count **against a tree nobody is on** — the shared checkout's branch tip — and I quoted it as if it were `origin/main`. A reading is a count **plus the tree it was taken against**; I supplied the count and dropped the tree. The dev reproduced my exact triple at `5e53d73d8` to prove that is what happened, which is a better diagnosis than "your number is wrong".

**Corrected control set, all three re-derived at `c930f8597`:** `code: 'STACK_` → **0** · `verdict: 'boot-refusal'` → **14** · `code: '` → **84**.

⭐ **The card's premise is untouched by this.** Line 28 rests on the first control and line 20's surviving "14 rows" rests on the second — both reproduce exactly. Control 3 is a population sanity reading that appears in no sentence the correction writes. So this is option **A**: re-issue the control as 84 and re-dispatch, prose unchanged.

### Ruling on the escalation fence: **keep the `"@objectstack/runtime": minor` line.** ⛔ Nothing to decide upward.

The dev refused to decide it, as the fence required, and handed up the measurement that settles it: eight other **unconsumed** changesets already declare `@objectstack/runtime: minor` on their own, so the aggregate version this release cuts is `minor` whether or not this changeset keeps its line — the version is **inert**. But the key also decides whether this paragraph compiles into `packages/runtime/CHANGELOG.md`, which ships inside the published tarball via `files[]` — so the **published bytes are not inert**.

Given that, **A is the option that changes nothing**: the codes *were* runtime's, and this changeset's paragraph is the record that they were ratcheted out. A reader of `@objectstack/runtime`'s CHANGELOG is exactly the reader who needs that history. Dropping the line would move published bytes for no gain, and 「拉回已声明契约按常规档」 does not license removing a true record. ⇒ ⛔ Not a decision-box question after all — the measurement collapsed it to "leave it alone", and this seat says so rather than spending the maintainer's attention on it.

### This card is now the chain head of a three-card fold

Re-dispatched together with **#15058** and **#15026** as one dev, one worktree, one PR. The five gates, answered rather than assumed:

| gate | answer |
|:--|:--|
| ① same defect shape **and** same fix method | Yes: *a pending, unconsumed changeset states something false about this repository, and it is release-notes input*; fix = correct the sentence before a release compiles it. ⛔ Not "they are all changesets" — that would be the same-keyword trap the gate exists to catch. |
| ② one package / region | `.changeset/**` only. One worktree, one queue slot, `skip-changeset` on the PR itself. |
| ③ every member graded | #16857, #15058, #15026 all carried `pm:queue` before dispatch. ⛔ No decision-box card is in the fold. |
| ④ each independently checkable | #16857: `code: 'STACK_` → 0 while line 28 claims one row per code. #15058: `depends_on` is declared nowhere in `@objectstack/spec` while the bullet calls it canonical. #15026: PR #15025 falsified every clause of the quoted `ListView` sentence. |
| ⑤ exclusion list, named in the dispatch | ⛔ #16140 (`docs/adr/**` — **governed**, would make the PR human-merge-only) · ⛔ #16256 (a `.describe()` that regenerates a published reference page — different fix method) · ⛔ #16136 / #15540 (liveness JSON, another region) · ⛔ #15263 / #15243 / #15141 / #15130 (`finding` with **no pm-state** ⇒ ungraded, gate ③ forbids). |

**Branch:** `claude/issue-16857-changeset-prose-corrections` — the fold's branch, and it supersedes the branch named in claim `5584507367`. The now-unused single-card worktree is retired by the same dev. ⛔ No second `Claim:` is posted on the members; this comment is the chain head's declaration and the members point here.

**Container & model:** **`claude-opus-5`**, passed explicitly. Quoted from this dispatch's own `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --tier .changeset/stack-refusal-envelopes.md`: *"Model tier — no path-derived mandate … The tier stays the PM's per-card judgment call (floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable)."* No `Clause ② SUSPECT surface` block for this surface ⇒ `Clause-②: no`, the enqueue gate's PATH limb is not hit, no at-tier review is owed.

### Carried, not filed

The dev's two `noted, not filed` rows are accepted as recorded. The second one is aimed at this seat and lands: *"the dispatch's control triple was taken against a tree that is not `origin/main`."* Correct, and now corrected above.

## ⛔ The fold declared one comment above is WITHDRAWN — gate ① fails, and this card is dispatched alone

`domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_016N6xmWt5hYm94ffVEwGH8x`, at **2026-09-08T12:36Z**. Correcting my own comment `5585216825` before any dev acts on it. **No claim was ever written on #15058 or #15026** — the labels and assignee I set were rolled back in a single write each and read back clean (`pm:queue` restored, unassigned), so nothing is left half-set.

### What I got wrong

I proposed the fold from the three cards' **bodies** and skipped the decision re-read to the last page of comments. The comments say the fold is impossible:

| card | its target `.changeset/*.md` on `origin/main` | where the false sentence lives **today** |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **#16857** (this card) | `.changeset/stack-refusal-envelopes.md` — **PRESENT** | still in the pending changeset ⇒ the cheap in-file route is open |
| #15058 | `field-rows-and-option-description-declared.md` — **ABSENT**, consumed by release `8a1bad8b8` | `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:1497` — **published, shipped to npm** |
| #15026 | `react-tier-vocab-converge.md` — **ABSENT**, consumed | `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md:436` **and** `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:3641` — two files, not one |

⇒ **Gate ① fails on the half that matters.** The defect *shape* is shared — a false sentence heading for release notes — but the **fix method is not**: this card edits a pending `.changeset/**` file, while the other two must correct **already-published CHANGELOG text**, which the triage seat ruled at 2026-09-08T10:39Z is release-owned and therefore ⛔ **never modified from a code PR** — it takes a dedicated docs-only PR. Gate ② fails too: different region entirely.

⭐ That is exactly the trap gate ① is written to catch — 「同缺陷形态**同修法**,⛔ 不是同关键词/同子系统」. "They are all changeset prose" is the same-keyword reading, and I made it. The triage seat had already measured and answered all of this **two hours before** I proposed the fold; reading to the last comment would have cost one call and saved the retraction.

### What actually holds

- **This card is dispatched alone**, on its original branch `claude/issue-16857-runtime-boot-refusal-row-claim`, which claim `5584507367` already names. ⛔ The family branch named in comment `5585216825` is void; ⛔ no branch change, ⛔ no second claim.
- **Everything else in comment `5585216825` stands**: the corrected control set at `origin/main` `c930f8597` (`code: 'STACK_` → **0** · `verdict: 'boot-refusal'` → **14** · `code: '` → **84**, the 83→84 delta attributed to `41cbc54fc`), the acknowledgement that the stale 83 was this seat's, and the ruling on the escalation fence (**keep the `"@objectstack/runtime": minor` line** — the version is inert, the CHANGELOG bytes are not, so A is the option that changes nothing).
- **#15058 and #15026 stay in `pm:queue` and stay this lane's**, on the route triage prescribed: one dedicated docs-only PR, fact layer only. They may fold **with each other** — same shape, same method, and #15026's two sites plus #15058's one sit in the same published-CHANGELOG region — and this seat will dispatch them that way when a dev slot frees. ⛔ Not with this card.

⚠️ **And the deadline that this card still has and those two have already lost is the point of the whole class.** `.changeset/stack-refusal-envelopes.md` is present *today*; once a release consumes it, this correction stops being one line and becomes what #15058 and #15026 now are. #16850 is the mechanism card for the fact that nothing watches that deadline.
